title: Highest temperature in London on August 22?
description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple sources points to a high of 20–21°C in Munich on August 22, 2026, driving the heavy weighting on those outcomes.** Official and model-based projections (including GFS and others) indicate mostly clear to partly cloudy skies after Friday’s widespread thunderstorms and rain, with westerly winds of 10–20 km/h limiting afternoon heating. This follows a cooler, unsettled pattern that has kept recent highs near or below seasonal norms.

The market-implied probabilities align closely with this: 21°C leads at 46.5% because it matches the most frequent point forecast across sources, while 20°C (19.5%) and 22°C (20.5%) capture the typical uncertainty range in maximum temperature verification. Historical averages for the date sit near 23.7°C, but the immediate post-frontal regime and moderate winds suppress the upside, keeping odds on 23°C or higher below 7% combined.

Traders are also pricing in limited variability from model spread, with no strong signals for either significant warming or further cooling. Upcoming official updates from agencies like the German Weather Service will refine the exact peak, but current conditions favor resolution near the 20–22°C cluster.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/zhengzhou/ZHCC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple meteorological sources indicate highs near 32°C in Zhengzhou on August 22, driven by typical late-summer subtropical high pressure and warm advection patterns across the North China Plain. Model consensus points to partly cloudy conditions with possible thundershowers that could cap peak temperatures through increased cloud cover and evaporative cooling, while humidity and light northeast winds sustain heat indices above observed air temperatures. Historical August averages of 31–33°C provide climatological context, with current data releases from regional observations showing no significant deviations from seasonal norms. Traders appear to weigh these near-term model outputs against resolution criteria tied to official daily maximum readings, favoring the 32°C threshold amid forecast uncertainty.
